headline: Plaintiff in Sayedee war crimes case buried at 2 AM after day-long tension in Pirojpur
summary: Freedom fighter Manik Pashari, plaintiff in a war crimes case against Delawar Hossain Sayedee, was buried late Saturday night. Local Jamaat activists reportedly obstructed his funeral and guard of honor ceremony throughout the day.
details: Freedom fighter Manik Pashari, the plaintiff in the 1971 war crimes case against former MP and Jamaat leader Delawar Hossain Sayedee, was buried at his home in Pirojpur at 2 AM on Saturday night. This followed a day-long period of tension surrounding his body.

Local Jamaat activists and supporters reportedly obstructed his funeral and the provision of a guard of honor for him as a freedom fighter since Saturday afternoon. This created significant unrest in the area.
At one point, the administration secretly provided the guard of honor. For security reasons, the body was also kept under the custody of the administration for some time.
Preparations for the burial, including digging the grave at Manik Pashari's home, began around 11:30 PM. The situation remained tense until the final rites were completed.
Pirojpur Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shafiqul Islam confirmed that the situation was brought under control. The burial was completed at his residence around 2 AM.

Manik Pashari filed the human rights violation case against Delawar Hossain Sayedee and four others at Pirojpur police station on August 12, 2009. This case was later merged with the main case against Sayedee at the International Criminal Tribunal.
caption:
Freedom fighter Manik Pashari, plaintiff in the Delawar Hossain Sayedee war crimes case, was finally buried at 2 AM after a day of intense tension in Pirojpur.

Freedom fighter Manik Pashari, the plaintiff in the 1971 war crimes case against former MP and Jamaat leader Delawar Hossain Sayedee, was buried at his home in Pirojpur at 2 AM on Saturday night. This followed a day-long period of tension surrounding his body.

Local Jamaat activists and supporters reportedly obstructed his funeral and the provision of a guard of honor for him as a freedom fighter since Saturday afternoon. This created significant unrest in the area.

At one point, the administration secretly provided the guard of honor. For security reasons, the body was also kept under the custody of the administration for some time.

Preparations for the burial, including digging the grave at Manik Pashari's home, began around 11:30 PM. The situation remained tense until the final rites were completed.

Pirojpur Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shafiqul Islam confirmed that the situation was brought under control. The burial was completed at his residence around 2 AM.

Manik Pashari filed the human rights violation case against Delawar Hossain Sayedee and four others at Pirojpur police station on August 12, 2009. This case was later merged with the main case against Sayedee at the International Criminal Tribunal.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh, Japan to sign $2B loan deals]] during PM Tarique Rahman's Tokyo visit
headline: Bangladesh, Japan to sign $2B loan deals during PM Tarique Rahman's Tokyo visit
summary: The proposed package includes budgetary support, infrastructure development, and cooperation in energy and maritime security, aiming to elevate bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership.
details: Bangladesh and Japan are set to sign memorandums of understanding (MoUs) for approximately $2 billion in loans and financial support during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s official visit to Tokyo from October 26 to 29. A summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is scheduled for October 27.

The proposed financial package is expected to cover budgetary support, infrastructure development, and cooperation in energy and maritime security. Around $300 million of this amount is specifically earmarked for budgetary support, according to diplomatic sources.

Japan is also anticipated to arrange an additional 1 trillion yen (approximately $6.36 billion) in private-sector investment in Bangladesh over the next five years. This initiative aims to bolster regional connectivity, particularly through the Moheshkhali-Matarbari Integrated Infrastructure Development Initiative (MIDI).

Under Japan’s Official Security Assistance (OSA) programme, Tokyo is likely to provide a 35-foot vessel to the Bangladesh Coast Guard. This follows the earlier handover of five patrol boats to the Bangladesh Navy, marking Bangladesh's first OSA project.

The visit is expected to elevate the relationship between the two nations to a comprehensive strategic partnership (CSP). This expansion will encompass cooperation in infrastructure, energy, regional connectivity, and investment.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam highlighted Japan's long-standing role as a major trade and development partner for Bangladesh. She expressed hope that the visit would attract fresh Japanese investment across various sectors, including technology, garments, education, and health.

Japan's broader vision for the region, the Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) initiative, will be a key focus, with efforts to counter Chinese influence. The Matarbari deep-sea port is central to this vision, designed for broader regional connectivity beyond bilateral use.
